NH3-plasmas can effectively passivate the GaAs surface and the high-k/GaN interface, thus reducing the interface-state density and the leakage current density.

N2 − and NH3-plasma treatments can passivate the high k/GaAs interface by introducing N, H, and NH species into the high-k/GaN interface, which can effectively reduce interface-state density, gate leakage current density, and capacitance equivalent thickness, and improve the equivalent dielectric constant.
the NH3-plasma-treated yittrium oxynitride can effectively passivate the GaAs surface and reduce the interface-state density.

the interfacial and the electrical properties of the high-k/GaN metal-oxide-semiconductors (MOS) with NH3-plasmatreated Y2O3 interfacial layer.
the interfacial passivization of GaAs MOS capacitors with YONI as the interfacial layer by N2 +/-/NH3-plasmas.

the interfacial quality and electrical properties of high-k/GaAS interface with yittria-oxynitridation, and the NH3-plasma is proved to be an effective treatment for the passivation of high-k/GasAs interface, which is beneficial to improve the interfacial properties and electrical performance of high-k/GASAs interface.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the NH3-plasma-treated Y-oxynitrides are promising interfacial passivates for GaAs MOSFETs.

the NH3-plasma-treated yittrium oxynitride is a promising interfacial layer for GaAs metal-oxidesemiconductor devices, which can effectively reduce the interface-state density and improve the electrical properties of the GaAs MOS devices.
NH3-plasmas treatment can effectively passivate the interfacial states and improve the interfacial quality in GaAs-based MOS devices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the NH3-plasma-treated high-k dielectric layer with high equivalent dielectric constant and low interface-state density would be promising for high-k gate dielectric in GaAs metal-oxidesemiconductor devices.
the NH3-plasma pretreatment can improve the quality of the high-k/GaN interface, which is beneficial for the high-k/Gan MOS devices.

N2 − plasma can effectively reduce the interfacial state density of the GaAs MOS structure, and NH3-plasma could further improve the electrical properties of the high-k/GaN MOS structure by passivating GaAs surface with H atoms and NH groups, thus providing more effective passivation for the high-k/Gallium arsenide interface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NH3-plasmatreated YON can be used as an effective passivation layer for GaAs MOS device.
the NH3-plasma-treated high-k layer is an effective interfacial passivating layer, which can be used to fabricate the high-performance metal-oxide-semiconductors with GaAs channel.
the N2 − plasma treatment can be replaced by the NH3-plasma one, which is easier to implement in the GaAs metal-oxidesemiconductor devices.
